poster.title: A Separation
poster.creator: Poster artist uncredited
poster.alt: A Separation English-language poster with a woman in a brown headscarf sharply focused in front of a softly focused bearded man, pale title lettering across the bottom and small reviews above.
poster.blurb: Two faces share the same space, but focus and direction keep them apart.

notes.title: Focus creates the separation
notes.body: The woman’s face is sharply defined while the man behind her is softer. Depth of field becomes a visual way to keep two close figures apart.

notes.title: Gazes do not quite meet
notes.body: Both faces look beyond the frame rather than toward each other. The composition offers proximity without a reciprocal exchange, leaving the relationship tense and unfinished.

notes.title: A restrained palette leaves room for expression
notes.body: Brown, cream and muted skin tones keep the colour range narrow. The pale title and small review text recede enough for the two expressions to carry the image.

studyData.intro: Two faces occupy nearly the whole sheet, but they are not equally sharp or equally close. Read the distance between them, the directions of their gazes and the quieter title before deciding what kind of separation the image suggests.

regions.label: The foreground face
regions.summary: A sharply focused face dominates the left.

sections.heading: The nearer plane of attention
sections.body: The foreground face shows clear eyebrows, eyes, lips and small changes in skin tone. It occupies more of the sheet than the face behind it. Dark fabric and hair frame its pale areas, making the expression readable without an isolated portrait border.

sections.heading: Describe before interpreting
sections.body: The mouth is partly open and the eyebrows are drawn together. Those are visible features; a precise emotion or spoken sentence is not. Different viewers may read concern, urgency or disagreement, but the study keeps those interpretations separate from the observable facial arrangement.

regions.question: Which facial details are clearest, and which disappear into shadow?

regions.label: A gaze beyond the frame
regions.kicker: A direction inside a close portrait
regions.summary: Two dark eyes point toward an unseen subject.

sections.heading: A direction inside a close portrait
sections.body: The dark eyes sit within a strongly lit face and look toward the right side of the image. The gaze does not directly address the viewer. Their small highlights and sharp outlines make them especially noticeable compared with the softer eye area of the person behind.

sections.heading: An absent destination
sections.body: Both faces appear oriented toward something beyond the frame, but the poster does not reveal what it is. That absence can make the viewer curious about a conversation or confrontation. It is a spatial clue, not evidence of a particular scene or person outside the crop.

regions.question: Do the eyes appear to meet yours, or look somewhere beside you?

regions.label: A partly open mouth
regions.summary: A small light opening interrupts the lower face.

sections.heading: A sharp local contrast
sections.body: The lips and pale teeth create a small, high-contrast area beneath the eyes. The opening is asymmetric, and shadow defines the lower lip and chin. This detail contributes to the sense of an active moment rather than a formally posed, closed-mouth portrait.

sections.heading: Speech without words
sections.body: The open mouth can suggest speech, surprise or a pause in breathing, but no speech is printed beside it. Supplying imagined dialogue would turn interpretation into invention. The poster lets a bodily cue raise a question while the title and reviews supply the only explicit verbal messages.

regions.question: What does the open mouth suggest, and what can it not prove?

regions.label: A dark frame of fabric
regions.summary: Brown folds surround the face and descend toward the title.

sections.heading: A frame within the crop
sections.body: The head covering surrounds the forehead, cheeks and neck in dark brown folds. Its irregular outer edge separates the foreground person from the warmer background and the second face. Beneath the chin, overlapping fabric makes a series of curved bands across the upper chest.

sections.heading: Clothing is not a complete identity
sections.body: The fabric is visible evidence of what is worn in this image. It does not establish a person’s beliefs, political position or emotional state. The film’s Iranian setting comes from the distributor’s record, rather than from treating one garment as a sufficient explanation of a culture.

regions.question: Where does fabric define the face’s outline most strongly?

regions.label: The softer face behind
regions.summary: A second portrait is partly hidden and less sharply focused.

sections.heading: Overlap and focus work together
sections.body: The foreground head covers part of the man’s left side. His face is also softer in focus, especially around the eyes and hair, while the beard forms a broad dark area. These two cues establish depth even though the faces are very close together on the sheet.

sections.heading: A marriage under strain
sections.body: Sony’s synopsis identifies the central conflict as a marriage in contemporary Iran: Simin wants to leave with Nader and their daughter, while Nader will not leave his father. That provides narrative context for the title. It does not make the two printed portraits a complete account of either person’s position.

regions.question: What tells you that this person is behind the foreground figure?

regions.label: The narrow interval between faces
regions.summary: A thin overlap zone separates two human planes.

sections.heading: Very little literal space
sections.body: The faces are not divided by a large blank gap. The nearer scarf overlaps the softer portrait, and a narrow band of shadow marks the boundary. The image therefore brings the people physically close on the page while still making their visual planes distinct.

sections.heading: A title tested against an image
sections.body: The word separation might lead a viewer to expect a wide physical gap. Here the distinction is made through focus, overlap and different facial directions. That tension is a plausible reading of the design; it is not proof of an intended metaphor documented by the poster’s maker.

regions.question: Is the separation created by empty space, by overlap or by focus?

regions.label: A small amount of warm ground
regions.shortLabel: A small amount of warm ground
regions.summary: Only narrow areas remain outside the portraits.

sections.heading: A setting almost removed
sections.body: Warm beige and brown areas remain above and beside the heads, but they do not describe a clear room or landscape. Most of the sheet is taken up by people and text. The crop gives little environmental information with which to explain the expressions.

sections.heading: A human-scale invitation
sections.body: This edition asks viewers to approach through faces rather than scenery, spectacle or a detailed plot summary. That is a visible campaign choice. It can make personal conflict seem central without proving that the film excludes broader social questions or that all viewers respond to the portraits in the same way.

regions.question: How much setting information has been excluded by this crop?

regions.label: Three small review groups
regions.summary: Fine pale writing forms a band over the heads.

sections.heading: A compressed top band
sections.body: Three groups of small pale text sit across the top, separated by narrow spaces. The lettering remains visible as a row of endorsements, but this 262-pixel-wide source cannot reliably reveal every word or attribution. The broad arrangement is more secure than a full transcript.

sections.heading: Borrowed voices above faces
sections.body: The review band brings external judgments into an otherwise intimate image. It can signal that others have valued the film before a viewer has formed an opinion. The study treats those endorsements as campaign material and does not promote unreadable fragments into verified quotations.

regions.question: Which matters first at this size: the words themselves or the fact that several voices are quoted?

regions.label: A small credential block
regions.summary: Festival information sits over the lower background portrait.

sections.heading: Information on a human surface
sections.body: The award and festival block occupies a narrow area on the right, over dark clothing and the lower part of the rear portrait. Small pale letters and laurel-like marks form a compact texture. Their position avoids the clearest foreground facial features while using the available darker ground.

sections.heading: A limit to reliable reading
sections.body: Some large words and marks can be recognized, but the source size does not support an exact inventory of every festival or prize here. The study therefore describes their function without inventing a complete list. A sharper original would be needed to verify a full transcription.

regions.question: How does placing text over a person change the way that portrait is read?

regions.label: A pale title across both portraits
regions.shortLabel: A pale title across both portraits
regions.kicker: A plain phrase over a complex image
regions.summary: The film name spans nearly the full width.

sections.heading: A plain phrase over a complex image
sections.body: The English title appears in large pale capitals near the bottom. Its relatively even strokes and straight baseline contrast with the detailed faces and folded fabric. The first word is short, while the longer second word stretches across both portrait areas, visually connecting them.

sections.heading: One line across two planes
sections.body: Because the title crosses the foreground and background figures, it can be read as a bridge over their difference or as another layer separating image from viewer. Both readings begin with its actual placement. Neither requires a claim that the designer intended one fixed meaning.

regions.question: Does the title feel like a divider, a bridge or both?

regions.label: The dense credit base
regions.summary: Very small production text finishes the sheet.

sections.heading: A shallow, dense band
sections.body: The production credits occupy several tightly packed lines beneath the main title. Their pale tone helps on dark clothing but becomes less distinct over lighter fabric. At this resolution they contribute a visible base of information without supporting reliable reading of every name.

sections.heading: Film record and poster evidence
sections.body: Sony’s official page supports the film’s identity and synopsis, but it does not establish the designer or exact printing date of this selected English-language image. Keeping those limits explicit prevents a film date, a distributor’s webpage or a familiar face from being mistaken for complete poster provenance.

regions.question: Where does the small writing become indistinguishable from image texture?

sources.title: Sony Pictures: A Separation
sources.summary: Verifies the film’s identity, contemporary Iranian setting and the Simin/Nader family conflict; does not verify this selected poster’s designer or exact printing date.

connections.label: Near but separate
connections.title: Focus makes two depths
connections.text: The woman’s sharp features sit directly in front of a softer male portrait. The difference in focus creates depth even where their silhouettes almost touch.

connections.label: Faces and quiet type
connections.title: Expression carries the centre
connections.text: The title spans the lower image while the two faces occupy the main field above it. Its muted pale tone keeps the expressions visually prominent.
